title: Conveyor scheduler for microburst mitigation and latency-weighted fairness
creator: Avery Chen
description: Implement a 'conveyor' prefill/decode scheduler that reduces tail latency for latency-sensitive microbursts while preserving throughput for bulk streams. The conveyor slices arriving requests into small conveyor belts that progress through prefill and decode stages with soft deadlines and credit-based fairness tokens. Integrates kernel-selection hints so short sequences take attention-optimized fastpaths and long sequences are packed for throughput kernels.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end P99 latency for small (<=64 tokens) requests reduced by >=15% under mixed load compared to baseline; 2) Overall token throughput change within +/-5% for typical production mix; 3) No starvation >2s observed for lower-priority workloads during 30-minute soak; 4) Observability: per-request phase timings, fairness token drops, kernel-hint events emitted to Console; 5) Canary rollout with automatic fallback policy implemented.
benchmarks: Staging perf run 2026-03-08: mixed workload (70% short chats <=64 tokens, 30% long generations). Baseline P99 short latency 420ms -> conveyor 345ms (-17.9%). Aggregate tokens/sec +3.4%. Memory overhead +2% due to conveyor metadata. Kernel hinting reduced attention-kernel invocations for long sequences by 22%.
tasks: Integrate fairness token accounting with quota service
Run extended soak on Dedicated cluster (staging)
Add Console charts and alerts for conveyor metrics
decisions: Use credit-based fairness (tokens) vs strict priority to avoid starvation.
Conveyor belts are time-sliced with progressive aging: belts that miss deadline get priority boost next cycle.
Kernel-hints implemented as lightweight enums attached to request descriptors; runtime will prefer attention-fastpath when hint == SHORT_SEQ.
Defer global autoscaler interactions until stable metrics are available; conveyor local scheduling only for now.
